The patient is a ___ year-old ___ man with a history of 
seizures, TIA, DM, HTN, and CKD, who is transferred from ___
___ with athetosis of the right hand.

He was admitted to the neurology stroke service given concern 
that athetosis represented an acute stroke.

MRI was done, read 
as negative, but on our stroke neurologists review, there was an 
acute subthalamic and ventrolateral thalamic stroke.

His stroke 
risk factors were evaluated: LDL 96, A1c 5.3%, echo 
unremarkable.

Lumbar puncture was done and was negative, 
including negative VDRL and Tb PCR.

Athetosis can also be 
caused by phenytoin (although not toxic) liver, thyroid (no 
evidence), electrolyte disturbance (no evidence).

Other 
considerations include Syndeham chorea, TB meningitis, HIV, and 
syphillis (all were negative except RPR).

His RPR and 
confirmatory FTA-Ab returned positive, but his VDRL was pending 
at time of discharge.

(At the time of this note, VDRL is 
negative).

We discussed the case with our ID colleagues and 
they felt that patient likely had prior exposure based on the 
low titer and positive Ab.

After additional review of his ___ record, he was 
admitted in ___ with GTC and partial complex seizures with 
left hemispheric seizures for which he was started on Keppra

We tapered off the phenytoin because it 
has been associated with choreo-athetosis.

We also increased his 
keppra to 1000mg BID to ensure he was covered for seizures.

His 
choreoathetosis did not improve with removal of his phenytoin.

Zyprexa was tried to decrease his choreoa-athetosis - however, 
the Zyprexa resulted in prolonged Qtc and was discontinued.
